newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIA Ltd, CapMAC wrap Asian collateralised bonds.
newsitem.headline: ASIA Ltd, CapMAC wrap Asian collateralised bonds.

text.p: Asian Securitisation and Infrastructure Assurance Ltd (ASIA) and Capital Markets Assurance Corp (CapMAC) said on Friday they have provided the first financial guarantee wrap for a collateralised bond obligation (CBO) consisting entirely of Asian corporate bonds.
The US$132 million issue comprises U.S. dollar-denominated corporate and infrastructure bonds of 10 Asian countries, excluding Japan, said Nils Dahl, director of ASIA Ltd.
"The bonds were all publically traded bonds that were purchased in the secondary market and repackaged," said Dahl.
ASIA Ltd and CapMAC have collaborated on the issue so that, with ASIA Ltd support, CapMAC was able to provide its AAA-wrap to US$112 million in senior bonds.
The bonds are rated AAA by both Moody's Investors Service and Standard and Poor's Corp.
The remaining US$20 million of the issue consists of unrated, subordinated bonds.
ASIA Ltd said its role in the transaction was to provide credit assessment and primary credit enhancement within the structure so that CapMAC could provide an overall guarantee.
The senior bonds have a legal life of 10 years and an average life of slightly more than six years, Dahl said. They pay a margin of 25 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The bonds were privately placed by Bear Stearns International. They will be listed in London.

The transaction, which was made through special purpose company Anfield Road 1 Ltd, also involved an interest rate swap that was provided by Bear Stearns Financial Products and guaranteed by CapMAC and ASIA Ltd.

Singapore-based ASIA Ltd was established with the support of CapMAC, the Asian Development Bank, the Government of Singapore Investment Corp and other Asian institutional investors as Asia's first financial guarantee company.
CapMAC is a U.S.-based monoline financial guarantee insurance company.
ASIA Ltd recently guaranteed the public issuance of US$225 million in five-year notes issued by Securitization and Infrastructure Funding Corp.
